summary: Staggered microstream shadowing causing dedicated GPU attach lag and autoscaler sluggishness
description: Customer reports sustained p95/p99 latency regressions on a dedicated pool during mid-day traffic. Symptoms include many short-lived microstreams (0.5s-2s) that remain attached for long tails, causing GPU slot hold and preventing new batched attaches. Autoscaler does not react fast enough due to smoothing and heartbeat thresholds, so throughput collapses and requests queue.
impact: Customer NimbleDocs experienced elevated token-generation latency (p99 ~2.3s -> 6.8s) and intermittent 503 attach failures for ~90 minutes. Impacted routes: /v1/chat/stream (batched route) and low-throughput async endpoints. Business impact: delayed document summarization pipelines and user-facing timeouts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a dedicated pool with mixed small-stream and medium-batch tenants in us-east-1
2) Simulate 2k short microstreams per minute (0.5s-2s) that keep socket open with sparse token progress
3) Interleave a medium-batch workload (batch_size 8-16) pinned to same pool
4) Observe attach latency, queue length, and autoscaler scaling decisions via /allocator telemetry
investigation_notes: Initial triage by support: confirmed dedicated pool attach_wait_queue growth correlates with burst of short streams from tenant 'nimbledocs'.
Hypothesis A: Small microstreams with long socket linger are fragmenting GPU slots — allocator counts connection as 'active' while actual token compute is negligible, blocking batched attaches.
Hypothesis B: Autoscaler smoothing (120s) + heartbeat grace prevents rapid pool expansion; combined with predictive shrink cooldown, capacity cannot absorb sudden medium-batch demand.
Telemetry: prefetched KV cache size for customer rose ~30% during incident; sidecar logs show repeated partial prefetch writes (likely mis-sized prompt sets).
Reproduced in staging with traffic shim: observed same attach queue growth when short-stream ratio > 65% and mean connection hold > 3s.
Checked GPU availability: physical GPU counts OK, but slot allocation refused due to active lease accounting (connections flagged as long-lived).
Correlation found with recent tenant client update rolling out keep-alive semantics — new SDK holds streams open between micro-requests leading to shadowing effect.
Linked allocator PR #4123 contains a telemetry change that will help differentiate 'compute-active' vs 'idle-socket' leases for future heuristics.

root_cause: A change in the customer's client SDK increased ratio of short-lived but socket-persistent microstreams. The allocator counted these as active leases, preventing efficient slot reuse and blocking batched attaches. The autoscaler's smoothing settings delayed capacity expansion, amplifying the throughput collapse.
resolution: Applied a temporary fix: enabled allocator feature-flag to expire idle socket leases after 1.5s of zero-GPU-compute and restarted sidecars on affected shards. Customer rolled back client SDK change. Autoscaler smoothing window reduced from 120s -> 45s for the pool as emergency measure. These mitigations restored throughput and reduced p99 latency back to baseline.
time_to_restore: ~42 minutes from mitigation deployment to stable p99 improvement
permanent_remediation: 1) Ship allocator PR to distinguish 'compute-active' vs 'idle-socket' leases and make expiry configurable per-pool (PR #4123).
2) Add new autoscaler policy mode 'fast-burst' for dedicated pools supporting high microstream ratios (configurable cooldowns and smoothing).
3) Create customer-facing guidance in docs: recommended client SDK patterns for short-interaction workloads and suggested pool sizing rules.
4) Add alerting: attach_wait_queue > 100 for >5min and prefetched_kv_growth >20% in 10min to create early warning.
5) Post-incident: schedule 2-week follow-up to monitor related pools and roll out allocator and autoscaler changes to regional clusters.
